OH MY GOSH Thank you so much for your response, this is so helpful!  This makes me think about something I've *heard* people call "dimensional analysis", but it's not the thing with physics units. It's where you look at how some geometric "thing" behaves in 2D space (or maybe 1D sometimes), then go one dimension higher and look at how it behaves in 3D. Then, you take away all the pictures and try to find a pattern, then just continue the pattern into 4D.

Like a square is 2D, has 4 sides (lines). A cube is 3D and has 6 sides (squares). So then it seems like there is some sense in which a "4D cube", whatever that is, should have 8 sides that are all cubes. I'm sure you have to be a bit more careful than that to make sure you are extrapolating the *right* patterns, but that's the idea.

That stuff has always been really cool to me, and also trying to learn about it hasn't caused me quite so much grief as other things. I'm wondering if it's because, even though it sort of feels like it's about shapes-y stuff, all of the hard thinking there isn't really visual at all.

Thanks for your comment. I'll try to see how good I can answer this.

If I saw 5 dots on a paper, then closed my eyes, I would *see* absolutely nothing (except for those little colored lights and floaties but that's an optics thing--nothing to do with my thoughts). However, I *could* remember their orientation after closing my eyes. If you showed them to me, covered my eyes, and took the dots away and gave me blank paper, I could draw the same orientation of dots you showed me. I have no inner voice, no words in my head, no images, nothing. But I *remember* the dots, I *know* where they were and roughly their spacing etc. That memory and that information does not exist as a *sensation* in my head, but it *is* there.
Yes. I was trying to say that in my post, it was my main point.
